decision: Use fetch wrapper instead of Hono RPC
alternatives: Hono RPC (type-safe but couples to backend)
openapi-fetch (OpenAPI-driven)
Plain fetch wrapper (backend-agnostic)
rationale: Frontend must work with both TypeScript (Hono) and Python (FastAPI) backends. A simple fetch wrapper with Zod validation achieves type safety without backend coupling.

alternatives: generic admin-only — every project inherits the sidebar shell
archetype as a closed hard-typed enum — forces the least-bad fit
presets + governed custom escape hatch
rationale: AI agents defaulted every product to an admin sidebar because the only reference slice was CRUD. Layer 0 archetype + focused/split shell presets + a *-list.tsx-gated CRUD contract + a governed custom escape hatch let an agent build non-admin UIs without regressing. Chosen via CED multi-model debate; all four traces converged on presets+escape.

decision: Use body-portaled fixed listboxes with a nested scroll lock
alternatives: portal inside transformed dialogs
body portal relying only on native overflow
manual wheel-to-scrollTop handling
body portal with viewport geometry and nested RemoveScroll
rationale: Dialog transforms break descendant fixed coordinates, while Radix modal scroll locks suppress native wheel and touch input on body portals. A no-isolation nested RemoveScroll composes with the active dialog lock and preserves native input without moving or clipping the panel.

decision: One error and session policy in the QueryClient caches, errors rendered inside the layout
alternatives: per-hook onError handling of 401
a fetch wrapper that redirects on 401
QueryCache and MutationCache onError plus defaultErrorComponent
rationale: Per-hook handling drifted (no hook handled 401) and a redirecting fetch wrapper cannot clear the query cache. The cache-level onError sees every query and mutation once, clears cached data from the lost session and returns to the same page after login; rendering errors per route keeps the menu and gives a retry that re-runs the loader without a reload. Loader prefetches ignore a CancelledError because React can hide a cached page mid-load and unsubscribe the only observer; the page refetches on mount.

decision: Suave as the default identity: one token block + one icon wrapper re-skin the app
alternatives: keep Aether (neutral black/white + Geist, indistinguishable from stock shadcn)
src/themes/<identity>.css files (blocked by INVARIANT #10: styles.css is the only CSS file)
identity block inside styles.css with semantic radius/shadow/density/motion utilities
rationale: Projects built from the skeleton all looked like default shadcn because the look lived in dark: overrides and rgba values inside components and the theme only varied --primary. Moving every visual value into one IDENTITY block (colors, fonts, radii, elevation, density, motion) and every icon import behind src/ui/icons.ts makes the look swappable per product, keeps shadcn token names so tweakcn/shadcn-create exports paste over it, and lets the design guard ban the generic tells (icon tiles, uppercase labels, gradients) instead of enforcing one aesthetic.

decision: The session check (authQueryOptions) runs without an AbortSignal and with networkMode 'always'
alternatives: catch CancelledError in the _authed beforeLoad and ask again
stop the pending screen from observing auth/me
drop the signal from the session query only
rationale: The _authed beforeLoad awaits the same ['auth','me'] fetch that the pending screen observes. When a query consumed its signal (or was paused offline), an observer unmounting mid-request cancels the fetch and the guard rejects with CancelledError, so a reload showed 'Algo salió mal' (30/50 reloads with a 500 ms auth/me, 0/50 after). Not reading the signal makes an unmount only stop retries; the api-client timeout still bounds the request. A retry in the guard would hide the race instead of removing it, and keeping the pending screen from reading the user would cost the layout its user menu.

decision: Better Auth's client lives in one file that exports a typed function per /api/auth endpoint, built on the vanilla client with the api-client as transport
alternatives: export the authClient from better-auth/react and call it from hooks
raw fetch to /api/auth/* through api.post
the vanilla client exported as is
rationale: The client's inferred type is too large to emit (TS7056, as on the API). One function per endpoint also makes the file the list the API's allowlist must serve. The vanilla client has no React hooks to tempt server state out of TanStack Query (INVARIANTS #9), and customFetchImpl routes it through api.send, so its calls keep the 15 s limit and the network-error shape. INVARIANTS #7 names the file as its only exception (ADR 0022).

decision: The router's parseSearch folds Better Auth's signed OAuth query into one opaque oauth_query param
alternatives: let oauthProviderClient read window.location.search
capture the query once at boot, before the router mounts
a custom parseSearch/stringifySearch pair for the whole app
rationale: The signed query repeats ba_param; on mount TanStack Router rewrites the URL and turns the repeated key into one JSON array, so the signature no longer verifies (unit test reproduces it). Capturing at boot breaks on reload. Folding at parse time keeps every other param's behavior, survives reload, and the login and consent pages post the value back as oauth_query.

decision: Changing a member's role looks up the membership id with GET /organization/list-members, filtered by user id
alternatives: add memberId to the REST team member view (shared schema and both adapters)
read the whole member list from Better Auth instead of REST
rationale: update-member-role takes a membership id and the REST team list is keyed by user id. One filtered lookup per change needs only an allowlist line on the API; the list keeps its REST paging, search and sort. If the team view gains memberId, the lookup goes.

decision: Slice pages outside the app shell (OAuth consent, CLI approval, invitation, no team yet) compose PublicLayout from layouts/ themselves
alternatives: the route renders PublicLayout and the slice renders only the card's content
a card shell inside the auth slice
rationale: Each state of these pages (loading, error, a used code, success) changes the card's title, description, footer and whether it is a form, and that choice lives in the slice component next to its hooks. Lifting it into the route would move the logic out of the slice; a shell inside the slice would duplicate the layout, which INV-100 forbids. Composing the one shell keeps INV-100: the layout is defined only in layouts/, and a slice uses it like any other import.

decision: Team bulk remove calls Better Auth's remove-member once per selected member and counts the failures
alternatives: useBulkDelete against the REST team bulk route (team writes now go through Better Auth)
a bulk remove endpoint on the API that wraps Better Auth
stop at the first failure
rationale: Better Auth's organization plugin has no bulk remove-member, and team writes go through it so its rules apply (the last owner stays). Promise.allSettled removes every member it can; the toast reads 'No se pudo quitar a N de M miembros' with the first failure's reason, the selection clears and the list refetches. INVARIANTS #107 names team as its exception to useBulkDelete.
